items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Spend is estimated once at 1960 and seeds the campaign's depletion reserve
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): "For depletion accounting, I would prefer if we retrofit this, and come to a sensible estimate at the very end of digitisation. For generation you are right in that keeping items abstract is best policy." So NO ACCUMULATOR IS ADDED anywhere in the history sim, and sprint 39's closed Empire span is NOT reopened.

WHY IT MATTERS. Ben, 2026-09-11, on what digitisation passes forward: "the main levers we pass are going to be about how much of easily accessible resource has been actually spent." The saturated corporate web forms around what is LEFT.

WHERE IT LANDS IS ALREADY BUILT, AND THIS IS THE ELEGANT PART. `tile_component::resource_remaining` (components.hpp) is a finite reserve, live, drawn down by extraction and tapering output as it empties -- and it is SEEDED AT GENERATION to richness x a reserve factor (tile_generation.cpp). The two economy phases set that seed instead of a constant. Ground worked for centuries hands the campaign a thinner reserve. No new field, no new accumulator, no change to the campaign's extraction loop.

THE PRICE OF RETROFITTING, STATED PLAINLY AND ACCEPTED. An estimate computed once at 1960 can NEVER BE CHECKED against what actually happened, because nothing recorded it. That makes it a STATED FORMULA rather than a measurement. THE FORMULA MUST THEREFORE BE WRITTEN DOWN AS ONE -- named inputs, named arithmetic, in DIGITISATION.md -- or it silently becomes a fudge factor nobody can audit. Writing it down IS the work; an unwritten estimate is the failure mode.

ITS INPUTS ARE THE ABSTRACT ONES THE SIM ALREADY HOLDS: how long ground was held and worked, its `dominant` region class, whether it industrialised and when, and the corridor throughput that ran off it (BL-940).

PARKED UNTIL DIGITISATION IS DESIGNED. DIGITISATION.md is a placeholder by Ben's ruling; this item is filed now so the decision is not lost, and it is NOT sprint 40 work.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised)
items.title: Wire the Exploration span into the wizard as its own round, and add a Digitisation placeholder
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13 (live review, resolving NR-847 and NR-857): flip world_params::exploration_sim_enabled to default TRUE, and wire the Exploration span into the wizard as its own round -- and add the Digitisation placeholder round in the same pass.

THE ROUND LAYOUT. The wizard's pass rounds today are Culture, Empires, Industrialisation (`wizard_pass_round_count = 3`, `wizard_round_count = 5` = 2 planetology + 3 pass, src/core/app.hpp). "Industrialisation" is the acknowledged stand-in for everything after 1200 CE, and NR-843 already named the fact that there are now FOUR phases after Culture (Empires, Exploration, Digitisation) where the wizard has one placeholder. THE FIX: insert a new "Exploration" round between Empires and the renamed "Digitisation" placeholder -- wizard_pass_round_count 3 -> 4, wizard_round_count 5 -> 6. "Industrialisation" becomes "Digitisation" in name and header text only; it stays the honest empty placeholder it already is (BL-914's pattern) -- Digitisation itself is not this item's scope.

THE GOLDEN FLIP. exploration_sim_enabled default false -> true (NR-847). This moves region::nation from the 1200 CE map to the 1660 CE one for every generated world, which re-baselines world_determinism's digests and any other pinned generation output. AUTHORISED (Ben, 2026-09-13) -- this is not a silent re-bless: rerun world_determinism and history_sim_harness, record old and new digests in the DEVLOG, and confirm no assertion beyond the digest VALUES itself breaks (determinism -- same seed, same result twice -- must still hold).

THE MISSING TAP (NR-857's core finding). hard_coded_world.cpp currently writes `be.prehistory_timelapse = as_timelapse(hs)` using `hs` (the EMPIRES state) and passes `/*tap=*/nullptr` for the Exploration call -- so even with the span running, nothing reaches the wizard's lapse-map renderer. Build a REAL era_timelapse for the Exploration span the same way `build_migration_timelapse` does for Culture (BL-919's function is the precedent: it rebuilds the culture/settlement record into the shared `era_timelapse` shape) -- call it something like `build_exploration_timelapse`, fed by `kepler_exploration_hs` and the polity/culture state at 1200 CE. Wire this round's tap through the same `progress->lapse_tap` publish path round 3 (Culture) and round 4 (Empires) already use, so BL-943's corridor/consolidation exemplars finally have real Exploration events to draw (NR-857's exact gap).

GENERALISE THE LAPSE MACHINERY FROM TWO ROUNDS TO THREE. `wizard_lapse_round_count = 2` (Culture, Empires) becomes 3 (Culture, Empires, Exploration) -- the Industrialisation/Digitisation placeholder stays NOT a lapse round, same as today. `verify_api.cpp`'s `history_run(which)` (0=Culture? check the actual mapping -- the comment says "0 = round 4 the migration, 1 = round 5 the history" so recheck against current round numbering after the Culture/Empires split) needs a third index. Any code keyed on `wizard_lapse_round_count` (loop bounds, per-round record storage) generalises the same way.

DONE WHEN: the wizard walks six rounds (System, Life, Culture, Empires, Exploration, Digitisation); the Exploration round runs its own pass on arrival and shows a real, populated time-lapse map (not an empty placeholder); BL-943's exemplars draw on real Exploration-span events; `docs/ai/ACTIONS.json` and `docs/ui/question_log.json` are updated for the new round; `scripts/verify/history_lapse_press.lua` (or a new sibling script) exercises the new round the way it exercises rounds 3 and 4 today; world_determinism and history_sim_harness are rerun and their movement recorded in the DEVLOG, not silently absorbed.

SEQUENCING NOTE: BL-948 (the lapse speed control) should land in the SAME pass or immediately after, since it touches the same round-rendering code and should apply uniformly to all three lapse rounds including this new one.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised)
items.title: A speed control (45s / 90s / 180s) on every lapse round's time-lapse, default 90 seconds
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13: time-lapses currently run too fast to observe what is happening. Target the FULL playback (start year to end year, unskipped) at 90 seconds by default, and add a speed-control element present in EVERY lapse round (Culture, Empires, and the new Exploration round from BL-946) offering three settings: 45 seconds, 90 seconds, 180 seconds -- the user can also already skip ahead or scrub via the existing playhead/scrubber, this control is about the AUTOPLAY rate, not a replacement for scrubbing.

WHERE THE RATE LIVES TODAY. Find whatever currently drives year-per-frame or year-per-second in `history_lapse.cpp`'s playback (a fixed constant, most likely) and make it a function of (span length in years) / (chosen duration in seconds), recomputed whenever the round's span or the chosen duration changes -- a round with a longer span at the same duration setting must move faster per frame, not take longer wall-clock time, since the target is WALL-CLOCK duration, not years-per-second.

THE CONTROL ITSELF. Three-way selector (45s / 90s / 180s), same visual language as other wizard toggles (Sparse/Lean/Standard on the main menu is the nearest precedent for a three-way radio-style control). Persisted per-session is fine; it does not need to survive a restart unless that's trivial. Update `docs/ai/ACTIONS.json` for the new control and `docs/ui/question_log.json` for the surface it lives on.

DONE WHEN: all three lapse rounds (Culture, Empires, Exploration) expose the same speed control; selecting 45s/90s/180s visibly changes the playback rate; the default is 90s; a live click confirms the control is reachable and does what it says.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised from NR-849)
items.title: Tune the road ladder's third rung so Post Roads actually fires on a sweep
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13, resolving NR-849: tune it now rather than wait for later waves. `post_roads_built` totalled 0 across every sweep run this sprint (8+ seeds) -- the third rung (Post Roads, EX-WY-1a) needs a polity to hold the tree node, sit on a tier-2 corridor, AND have enough treasury simultaneously, and that conjunction never occurred. Lower `post_road_treasury_cost` (find the exact constant name in history_sim.cpp, landed with BL-940) and/or the tier-2-corridor-uses threshold that gates eligibility, and re-sweep (`exploration_sweep`) to confirm the rung fires in a meaningful share of worlds without becoming trivial (every corridor promoting immediately would be as uninformative as none ever doing so). Measure before and after, report both.

DONE WHEN: a sweep shows `post_roads_built` > 0 in a clear majority of seeds (not 0/N, not automatically N/N), and `treasury_spent_on_roads` correlates sensibly with the polities that built one.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised from NR-855)
items.title: Push the near/far cost split further so the displacement reading reliably clears its own bar
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13, resolving NR-855: push further rather than accept 0.88 as the resting state. BL-941's deterrence (Ceiling/Alarm at polity grain, wired into `treaty_value_q`'s near-home Alarm bonus and a flat `treaty_far_penalty_q` for distant pairs) moved the median displacement ratio from 0.01/0.16 up to 0.88 across a 3-seed sweep -- real progress, one seed already cleared 1.0, but the median has not. Strengthen the SAME mechanism rather than inventing a second one: widen the gap between the near-home Alarm bonus and the far-away penalty (both already exist in history_sim.cpp from BL-941), and/or extend Alarm's read of visible capability (standing army + navy) to weight more heavily on a longer-held border. Re-sweep at a WIDER seed count (16, not 3, per NR-855's own note that 3 seeds was chosen for runtime, not confidence) before judging the reading settled either way.

Do not touch the non-aggression block itself (BL-933) or the ratio's own definition (BL-948's operationalisation, confirmed correct by Ben 2026-09-13) -- this item is about the deterrence STRENGTH, not the measurement or the blocking mechanism.

DONE WHEN: a 16-seed sweep shows the median displacement ratio clears 1.0, conflict still persists (reading 2 stays green -- total conflict well above zero), and the change is a measured strengthening of BL-941's existing mechanism, not a new one bolted on.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised from NR-856)
items.title: Reading 3's "strongest realms" metric moves from region count to treasury/throughput rank
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13, resolving NR-856: change the ranking metric before concluding the creed mapping itself needs revisiting. Reading 3 ("both strategies pay") ranked a world's "strongest realms" by region count, which structurally favours EXPANSION over consolidation -- a consolidator by definition holds the SAME ground worked harder, so it can never outrank an expansionist on a region-count axis regardless of how strong its creed-derived disposition actually is. Change the ranking to something consolidation-sensitive: treasury (BL-932) and/or corridor throughput (BL-940) rank, or a composite, rather than region count alone. Re-sweep (wider than 3 seeds -- NR-856 flagged the sample as too small either way) and report whether a consolidator now appears among the strongest realms on some seeds.

Do NOT touch the Empire-phase creed axes (zeal/dominion/sea_legs_q) themselves in this item -- if the new metric STILL shows no consolidator ever qualifying, that is the evidence needed to justify BL-942's own named upstream fix as a SEPARATE, later item, not something to force here.

DONE WHEN: reading 3 ranks realms by treasury/throughput instead of region count, and the sweep's reported finding (consolidators appear now, or they genuinely still do not even on a fair metric) is stated plainly either way.
